bill.title: FIND Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.

industries.rationale: The bill directly protects firearm manufacturers, dealers, and trade associations from discrimination in federal contracting.
Banks and financial institutions that provide services to federal contractors would be affected if they maintain policies restricting business with firearm entities.
Defense contractors frequently hold federal contracts and may need to review policies regarding firearm-related business relationships.
Insurance companies that contract with the federal government would need to ensure their underwriting policies do not discriminate against firearm businesses.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit federal agencies from awarding contracts to companies that discriminate against firearm manufacturers, dealers, or trade associations. Contractors would be required to certify they have no policies that discriminate against firearm-related businesses and will not adopt such policies during the contract term. The requirement would apply to both prime contractors and subcontractors, with penalties for violations, but would not apply to sole-source contracts.

plain.whoItTouches: People who own or buy guns.

bill.title: Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-69.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects dairy producers and processors by expanding the types of milk schools may purchase and serve.
Schools participating in the lunch program face new training requirements and changes to meal planning and procurement rules.
Food service companies and suppliers to school meal programs would adjust product offerings to meet the expanded milk and nondairy beverage options.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would allow schools participating in the National School Lunch Program to offer whole milk and 2% milk to students, in addition to the low-fat and fat-free options currently required. It would expand nondairy milk alternatives, permit parents (not just doctors) to request milk substitutes for students with dietary restrictions, and exclude milk fat from saturated fat limits in school meals. The bill also requires annual food allergy training and certification for school food service staff.

plain.whoItTouches: Parents of young children. People who use food aid.

bill.title: Combating Organized Retail Crime Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill directly addresses organized theft targeting retail operations and e-commerce platforms.
The bill explicitly covers theft from interstate and foreign shipments, affecting logistics and shipping companies.
The bill addresses online marketplaces and social media platforms where stolen goods are sold, potentially creating new compliance obligations.
The bill expands money laundering statutes to cover prepaid cards and gift cards, affecting payment processors and card issuers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands federal authority to prosecute organized retail theft and supply-chain crime. It allows prosecutors to aggregate the value of stolen goods over a 12-month period to meet felony thresholds, makes these offenses predicate crimes for money laundering charges, and authorizes asset forfeiture. The bill also creates a temporary coordination center within the Department of Homeland Security to help federal agencies work together on these cases.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who uses the internet.

bill.title: CARE Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance. (Sponsor introductory remarks on measure: CR S7964)

industries.rationale: The bill creates a new Medicare payment stream for ground ambulance services that do not result in transport, directly affecting ambulance operators' revenues and service models.
Medicare payment policy changes for emergency medical services affect the program's costs and may influence private insurers' coverage decisions for similar services.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs Medicare to test a five-year program that would pay ambulance services even when they respond to an emergency call but do not transport the patient to a hospital. Payment rates would generally match what Medicare currently pays when a patient is transported. The Government Accountability Office would study how the program affects Medicare beneficiaries' access to emergency medical services and their health outcomes.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who sees a doctor or pays for care.

bill.title: ABC Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.

industries.rationale: Streamlined administrative processes for Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP may affect how providers interact with patients' caregivers and handle eligibility documentation.
Changes to Medicare and Medicaid administrative processes could affect insurers participating in these programs and their coordination with caregivers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs federal agencies to review and simplify the paperwork and application processes for Medicare, Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program, and Social Security. The goal is to reduce the burden on family caregivers by eliminating duplicative forms and streamlining eligibility procedures across these programs. Agencies must gather input from caregivers and state organizations, make improvements, and report their progress to Congress.

bill.title: Fair Access to Banking Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates how banks and credit unions may deny financial services to customers.
Digital asset firms have frequently reported being denied banking services, making them likely beneficiaries of fair-access requirements.
Firearms businesses have reported service denials from banks citing reputational risk, which this bill would prohibit.
Cannabis and related businesses have faced banking access challenges that this bill's requirements could address.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would restrict banks, credit unions, and payment card networks from refusing service to customers who comply with the law. Financial institutions could only deny service based on documented, quantitative risk standards set in advance, and could not cite reputational concerns as a reason. Violations would trigger penalties including loss of federal deposit insurance, exclusion from electronic payment systems, and potential civil lawsuits by affected customers.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone with a bank account, a loan or savings.

bill.title: Laken Riley Act
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-1.

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new detention mandates on DHS and creates liability exposure for federal agencies, while authorizing state governments to bring suit over immigration enforcement.

The bill creates new grounds for state litigation against the federal government and expands detention requirements, generating demand for legal services in immigration and intergovernmental litigation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain certain non-citizens who are in the country unlawfully and have been arrested for or charged with crimes including burglary, theft, assault on law enforcement, or offenses causing death or serious injury. It also allows state governments to sue the federal government if immigration enforcement decisions or failures—such as releasing detainees, not conducting required asylum interviews, or violating parole limitations—cause harm to the state or its residents, including financial harm exceeding $100.

plain.whoItTouches: People applying to live here, and their families here. People applying to come here, and their families here.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects rubber tire manufacturers by blocking new emission standards that would impose regulatory obligations on their facilities.
Tire manufacturers supply the transportation sector, and regulatory costs or compliance changes could affect tire pricing and availability.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would block an Environmental Protection Agency rule that sets emission standards for hazardous air pollutants from rubber tire manufacturing facilities. The EPA rule, published in November 2024, was designed to regulate emissions from the rubber processing part of tire manufacturing. If this resolution passes, that EPA rule would be nullified and would have no legal effect.

bill.title: Rural Development Hospital Technical Assistance Program Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry.

industries.rationale: The bill directly targets rural hospitals, providing them with technical assistance, training, and support for operational and financial improvements.
The program explicitly includes increasing telehealth capabilities as a development need, which would affect broadband and telecommunications infrastructure providers serving rural hospitals.
The bill addresses acquiring and upgrading health care information systems including electronic health records, which would involve technology vendors and IT service providers.
The program covers technical assistance for constructing, expanding, and modernizing health care facilities, which would involve construction and engineering firms.

bill.plainSummary: This bill formally establishes a technical assistance program within the Department of Agriculture to help rural hospitals (in areas with 50,000 or fewer residents) improve their operations and finances. The program would provide training and support to help these hospitals modernize facilities, expand telehealth, upgrade information systems, and navigate USDA loan and grant programs. Priority would go to hospitals already participating in certain USDA rural assistance programs, and USDA would report annually to Congress on the program's results.

plain.whoItTouches: Farmers, and anyone who buys food.

bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management relating to "Protection of Marine Archaeological Resources".
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-3.

industries.rationale: The resolution directly reduces regulatory reporting requirements for oil and gas lessees and operators conducting offshore exploration and development.
Archaeological preservation and cultural heritage organizations have a direct stake in rules governing protection of marine archaeological resources.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would undo a Bureau of Ocean Energy Management rule that requires oil and gas companies to submit archaeological reports with every exploration or development plan for offshore drilling. If passed, the bureau could only require such reports when a regional director has specific reason to believe archaeological resources might be present in the area. The change would reduce the documentation burden on companies seeking to drill on the Outer Continental Shelf.

bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Department of Energy relating to "Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Consumer Gas-fired Instantaneous Water Heaters".
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 12.

industries.rationale: Manufacturers of gas-fired instantaneous water heaters would be directly affected by the nullification of energy efficiency standards that govern their product design and compliance costs.
Natural gas suppliers have a stake in standards that affect the efficiency and market competitiveness of gas-fired appliances versus electric alternatives.
Energy efficiency standards for gas appliances can influence the relative market share of gas versus electric water heating systems.
Contractors and builders who install water heaters would face different product availability and compliance requirements depending on whether the standards remain in effect.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would overturn a Department of Energy rule issued in December 2024 that set new energy efficiency standards for gas-fired instantaneous water heaters (commonly called tankless water heaters). The DOE rule required these appliances to meet stricter energy conservation requirements. If this resolution passes, the new standards would be nullified and would not take effect.

bill.title: HALT Fentanyl Act
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-26.

industries.rationale: The bill changes registration and licensing requirements for pharmaceutical researchers conducting controlled substance research and affects the regulatory classification of chemical substances.
The bill establishes new criminal penalties and quantity thresholds that will affect prosecution and defense of drug trafficking cases.
Universities and research institutions conducting controlled substance research would be subject to the new registration processes and requirements established by the bill.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would permanently classify all fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I controlled substances, meaning they would be treated as having high abuse potential and no accepted medical use. It sets the same criminal penalties and quantity thresholds for fentanyl-related substances as currently apply to fentanyl analogues. The bill also creates a streamlined registration process for researchers studying Schedule I substances and relaxes some requirements for research facilities working with controlled substances.

plain.whoItTouches: People caught up in the criminal law, and victims of crime.

bill.title: LEOSA Reform Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: Organizations focused on gun rights and gun safety advocacy have direct stakes in legislation that changes concealed-carry rules and school-zone firearm restrictions.
The bill expands where concealed firearms may be carried, potentially affecting demand for firearms and ammunition among law enforcement and permit holders.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would allow certain current and retired law enforcement officers to carry concealed firearms in more places, including school zones, national parks, and some federal buildings open to the public. It would also permit people with state concealed-carry permits to carry firearms in school zones. States would gain flexibility to reduce how often retired officers must requalify to maintain their carry privileges.

plain.whoItTouches: People who own or buy guns. Police officers, and the people they stop.

bill.title: Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Committee on Veterans' Affairs. Hearings held. Hearings printed: S.Hrg. 119-35.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects the National Instant Criminal Background Check System used by licensed firearm dealers and importers.
Organizations focused on Second Amendment rights and veterans' advocacy have a direct stake in policies governing firearm access for veterans.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prevent the Department of Veterans Affairs from sending information about veterans or their beneficiaries to the national firearm background-check database solely because they have someone appointed to manage their benefits. The VA could still share such information if a court has found the person to be a danger to themselves or others.

plain.whoItTouches: People who own or buy guns. Veterans and their families.

bill.title: Pregnant Students’ Rights Act
bill.latestActionText: Cloture on the motion to proceed to the measure not invoked in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 47 - 45. Record Vote Number: 12. (CR S286)

industries.rationale: The bill imposes new disclosure and information requirements on institutions of higher education participating in federal student aid programs.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would require colleges and universities that receive federal student aid to provide information to students about resources and accommodations available for carrying a pregnancy to term and caring for a baby after birth. Schools would need to list both on-campus and community resources, explain available accommodations for pregnant and parenting students, and provide information on how to file discrimination complaints related to a student's decision to continue a pregnancy.

plain.whoItTouches: College students, and their families.

bill.title: Protecting Access for Hunters and Anglers Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects manufacturers and sellers of lead ammunition by limiting federal authority to regulate their products on public lands.
Manufacturers of fishing tackle containing lead would face fewer potential federal restrictions on their products' use.
Sporting goods retailers selling lead ammunition and tackle would benefit from reduced regulatory uncertainty around these product lines.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prevent three federal agencies—the Fish and Wildlife Service, Bureau of Land Management, and Forest Service—from banning or regulating the use of lead ammunition or fishing tackle on federal lands and waters. The agencies could still impose restrictions in specific locations if they determine, based on field data from that site, that lead use is the primary cause of a wildlife population decline and the state agrees to the regulation. Certain existing regulations would remain in place.

plain.whoItTouches: People who live near or work on federal land.

bill.title: Making National Parks Safer Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 469.

industries.rationale: The bill mandates installation of Next Generation 911 systems, which are internet-based telecommunications infrastructure that telecom providers typically supply and maintain.
NG911 systems are digital, internet protocol-based platforms requiring software, hardware, and IT services for implementation and operation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the National Park Service to assess the current state and costs of upgrading emergency call centers in national parks to Next Generation 911 systems. Based on that assessment, the Park Service must then develop a plan to install these modern, internet-based 911 systems at park emergency communications centers.

plain.whoItTouches: People who visit public land, and people who live beside it.

bill.title: Firearm Access During Shutdowns Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects firearm manufacturers and dealers by ensuring background checks and export licenses continue to be processed during shutdowns.
The bill changes staffing and operational requirements for FBI, ATF, Commerce, and State Department employees during government shutdowns.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires certain federal firearms-related operations to continue during government shutdowns. It designates background-check processing by the FBI, enforcement activities by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and firearm export-license processing by the Commerce and State Departments as essential services. Employees performing these functions would be classified as excepted workers who must report during a shutdown.
